title: Re-chock two panes standing in a rack when there is only one prop block to hold them
instruction: Both acrylic panes in the rack need a new beech chock between the pane and its stop block: fit one to the pane the prop block is holding, replace the split red chock on the other, and finish with the prop block and the red chock away from the rack. Do not lift the panes or let either one fall.
context: Sheet material stored on edge falls flat the moment nothing is in front of it, and a fallen pane is a cracked pane or a crushed hand. A chock only counts in front of its stop block, where there is room for one chock, so the split chock has to leave that place before the new one goes in, and something has to hold the pane meanwhile. The rack has one prop block for that, and it starts at the other pane: it can leave that pane only once its new chock is in, and each arm reaches only its own side of the rack, so the prop has to change hands on the way. Only the outcome is scored, so any other way of keeping both panes held throughout counts the same.
setup: Station table; x is the distance in front of the line joining the two arm bases, y is left (+) or right (-) of the midline between them. Fixed rack of painted steel: a back fence 56 cm long, 2 cm deep x 3 cm tall, centred on the midline with its front face at x = 37.5 cm; a strip 56 cm long, 0.7 cm deep x 0.4 cm tall, lying against the foot of the fence; and two stop blocks, each 7 cm long x 1.5 cm deep x 1.5 cm tall, with their rear faces (towards the fence) at x = 30.3 cm, centred at y = +22.5 cm and y = -22.5 cm. Two clear acrylic panes, each 16 cm long x 7 cm tall x 1.6 cm thick, 0.20 kg, stand on edge parallel to the fence with their rear face 1 mm from it, centred at y = +18 cm and y = -18 cm; the rear 0.6 cm of each pane's thickness sits on the strip and the front 1.0 cm overhangs it, so each pane leans forward onto whatever is in front of it. The front face of an upright pane is at x = 35.8 cm, 5.5 cm from its stop block. Prop block: oak, 4.5 cm deep x 5 cm wide x 9 cm tall, 0.15 kg, standing on the table against the front face of the left pane, centred at y = +13 cm (beside the left stop block's line, not in it). Red chock: pine painted red, 4 x 4 x 9 cm tall, 0.10 kg, standing against the front face of the right pane, centred at y = -22.5 cm, in line with the right stop block. Two new chocks: beech, 4 x 4 x 9 cm tall, 0.10 kg each, standing with their centres at x = 18 cm, y = +22.5 cm and y = -22.5 cm. Every loose block is square to the rack. Three distractors lie behind the rack, loose, and are not part of the task: a red ceramic mug (11.4 x 9 x 8 cm with handle, 0.30 kg) centred at x = 48 cm, y = +24 cm; a roll of clear tape (10 cm across, 5 cm high, 0.06 kg) lying flat, centred at x = 49 cm, y = -24 cm; and a Phillips screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 3.4 cm handle, 0.10 kg) lying left to right on the midline at x = 48 cm. Two arms with parallel grippers, bases at x = 0, y = +30.5 cm and y = -30.5 cm.
scoring: 0 if at any time either pane tilted more than 30 degrees from upright or its lowest point was more than 2 cm above the top of the strip; this is not undone by a good final state. Otherwise 0.5 for each pane that ends chocked, which needs all of: (a) the pane at rest, within 10 degrees of upright, with its rearmost point no more than 0.7 cm in front of the fence (still over the strip); (b) a new beech chock at rest, within 10 degrees of upright, its underside no more than 0.5 cm above the table, lying between that pane's stop block and the pane (no part of it nearer the arms than the stop block's rear face or farther than the pane's centre plane) and, measured along the rack, entirely within the stop block's 7 cm length and within the pane's length; (c) no part of the prop block or of the red chock within 3 cm of the pane, measured in plan between their outlines. So 0 at the start, for doing nothing and after any fall or lift; 0.5 for one pane finished; 1.0 for both. A new chock standing against a pane anywhere other than in front of its stop block earns nothing for that pane. The distractors are ignored.
reset_notes: Stand each pane back on the strip against the fence while holding it, set the prop block against the left pane and the red chock against the right pane, then let go; return the new chocks to their marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena (PhysX 240 Hz, 20 Hz control), calibrated YAM station replica. Rack, panes, prop and chocks are rigid boxes; the mug, tape and screwdriver are NVIDIA SimReady props. Friction is uniform and high (1.2/1.0), there is no force sensing and nothing cracks, so a fall is judged by a pane's tilt. The panes are small offcuts, opaque pale blue for visibility. A narrow strip under each pane's rear makes an unsupported pane tip at once, standing in for the knocks that topple real ones.
